errors.text_span: with numerical labels indicating counts or weights for each category
errors.evidence: The numerical labels represent percentages, as the main categories in each chart sum to 100. Describing them as 'counts or weights' is incorrect and misses this key detail.

errors.text_span: The left chart, "AttentionInfluence," shows a total of 14 major categories, including "Education" (25), "Teaching & resources" (15), "Science & technology education" (10), "Health & Medicine" (22), "Diseases" (11), "Science" (15), "Animal & Plant" (13), "Medical" (6), "Nutrition" (5), "Historical review" (7), "Society & culture" (10), "Events & people" (6), "Infor tech" (5), and "Materials" (2), with smaller sub-categories like "Engineer" (12), "Fin & Law" (3), "Manage" (2), "Policy" (1), "Emerging tech" (4), and "Tech & Society" (8) branching out from the inner ring.
errors.evidence: The description completely misinterprets the hierarchical structure of the chart. It conflates the 6 inner-ring parent categories (e.g., 'Education', 'Health & Medicine') with their outer-ring sub-categories (e.g., 'Teaching & resources', 'Diseases'), presenting them as a flat list of 'major categories' and 'smaller sub-categories' without describing the parent-child relationships. For example, it lists 'Education' (25) as major, and its components 'Teaching & resources' (15) and 'Science & technology education' (10) also as major.
The chart does not contain a category named 'Tech & Society'. The label in the chart is 'Tech & Engineer', and its value is 12 in the left chart and 8 in the right chart.

errors.text_span: The right chart, "FineWeb-Edu Classifier," displays 11 major categories, including "Education" (38), "Teaching & resources" (17), "Science & technology education" (19), "Health & Medicine" (19), "Diseases" (10), "Nutrition" (7), "Medical" (2), "Animal & Plant" (12), "Science" (15), "Historical review" (12), and "Society & culture" (5), with smaller sub-categories such as "Events & people" (2), "Infor tech" (3), "Materials" (3), "Emerging tech" (4), "Manage" (1), and "Tech & Society" (8) also shown.
errors.evidence: Similar to the left chart's description, this section misrepresents the hierarchical structure by mixing parent categories (inner ring) and sub-categories (outer ring) into confusing lists of 'major' and 'smaller' categories, failing to describe the actual relationships.

errors.text_span: "Manage" in dark red, "Policy" in dark red
errors.evidence: The categories 'Manage' and 'Policy' are in the 'Fin & Law' group, which is colored cyan/light blue, not dark red.

The 'Nutrition' category is part of the 'Health & Medicine' group and is colored light blue, not a general 'blue'. The description correctly identifies 'Diseases' and 'Medical' as light blue, so this is an inconsistency.
The 'Animal & Plant' category is part of the 'Science' group, which is colored a pink/red color, not 'dark red'.

The color for the 'Fin & Law' group is a distinct cyan, which the description later refers to as 'light blue' for other categories. Calling it simply 'blue' is imprecise and inconsistent, especially when a separate 'light blue' color is used for the Health group.
There is no standalone 'Engineer' category. The category is 'Tech & Engineer', and it represents a parent group in the inner ring.

errors.text_span: The segments appear to be ordered in descending size, with the largest categories (Education, Teaching & resources, and Science & technology education in the right chart) placed prominently at the top.
errors.evidence: The segments are not ordered strictly by descending size. For example, in the left chart, 'History & Society' (23) appears after 'Science' (15). Stating they 'appear' to be ordered is a weak hedge for an incorrect observation.
